LLM auditresponse for open-webui.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The script `open-webui.sh` is a simple wrapper that launches an Electron application with predefined flags. It uses `exec` to run the system-installed Electron binary with the bundled ASAR application file located at `/usr/lib/open-webui/app.asar`. The command-line arguments passed to Electron are explicitly defined and serve legitimate purposes related to Wayland support, sandboxing limitations, and input method functionality.

All flags used are standard Electron runtime options. The `--no-sandbox` flag is documented with a rationale: avoiding issues with shared memory in `/tmp` that can cause rendering problems. While disabling the sandbox reduces security isolation, this is acknowledged in the comment and aligns with upstream behavior (as noted regarding v0.0.15). There are no signs of obfuscated code, network requests, or unexpected file operations. The script does not download, execute external payloads, or exfiltrate data.

The use of `"$@"` is a shell-escaped form of `"$@"`, which safely passes through all original command-line arguments. Despite the unusual encoding, it is functionally equivalent and not malicious in this context. The script operates within expected packaging norms for desktop applications on Linux.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Wrapper script with justified Electron flags, no malicious behavior
</summary>
</security_assessment>

No network requests, dynamic downloads, or execution of fetched code occurs during the package() function. The dependencies are standard for Electron-based applications. The optdepends on `xdg-desktop-portal` is reasonable for theme integration. There are no signs of obfuscation, data exfiltration, or unauthorized system modifications.
</details>

</details>
